tokenizer.name: cl100k_base
tokenizer.counter: uint32 token buffer; ordinary text; checked against encode_ordinary
tokenizer.mode: ordinary text; special-token-looking strings count as literal text

method.totals: Sum of complete, independently tokenized category files. Per-line token counts are not substituted for file counts.
method.equivalent_content: Every delivered FFL 3 row is compared byte-for-byte after canonical expansion with the corresponding original FFL 2 row. JSONL contains those same seven fields c,e,o,p,q,r,s with compact one-letter keys and no derived hash IDs.
method.included: All shipped FFL headers, comments, defaults, evidence, qualifiers, footers and final line endings.
method.excluded: Graph inspection copies, images, documentation, schema/reader instructions, original source binaries, resolved source evidence text, and model request/response wrappers.
method.contexts: Six fixed subject/ancestor selections; full named FFL 3 including comments/footer, equivalent FFL 2, and seven-field canonical JSONL. Overlap between selections is retained; example totals are not a new knowledge census.
method.rates: Token savings = (baseline-current)/baseline; whole-set tokens/fact = sum(tokens)/sum(facts). Ratios are not unweighted averages of category rates.

limits: These measure representation efficiency, not LLM answer accuracy or clinical completeness.
The JSONL baseline is an equivalent fact serialization, not the original PDF/ZIP package. Other encodings may use fewer tokens.
cl100k_base is a fixed benchmark; other tokenizers and request wrappers give different counts. No API price or billed-token claim is made.
Selected subject contexts are illustrative, can overlap, and do not establish complete guideline applicability. The 8,192-token allowance is a comparison threshold, not a model recommendation.
